correctness.rationale: For iid vectors, mean squared pair distance is twice the trace covariance. Dirichlet \((1,1,1)\) barycentric moments give the interior value \((a^2+b^2+c^2)/18\). Weighting the three uniform edge-segment moments by side length gives the boundary value \((a^3+b^3+c^3+3abc)/(6(a+b+c))\). Standard triangle identities yield the stated \(s,R,r\) formulas. Subtracting and setting \(x=s-a,y=s-b,z=s-c>0\) gives an explicit polynomial with only positive coefficients, proving strictness. Fresh independent numerical evaluation on three scalene/isosceles test triangles reproduced the gap identities; the universal proof is symbolic.

originality.rationale: The accessible Lotnikov abstract treats the Zaporozhets–Tarasov mean-distance program and states a stronger triangle result in its first-moment context, but does not expose the audited \(p=2\) formulas. Tokmachev proves all moments under planar interior/boundary centroid coincidence; a triangle satisfies that centroid hypothesis only in the equilateral case, so it does not cover generic triangles. Exact formula searches returned the assigned finding rather than an older arbitrary-triangle boundary second moment. Full texts of the two recent arXiv papers were not obtained through the open route, and the combined authorized fallback attempt was safety-blocked and not retried; this remains a residual risk.

final_claim: For every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle, two independent area-uniform points have mean squared distance \((s^2-4Rr-r^2)/9\), two independent arclength-uniform boundary points have mean squared distance \((s^2-3r^2)/6\), and the exact positive gap is \((s^2+8Rr-7r^2)/18\).
limitations: Only squared Euclidean distance on triangles is treated.
